steps.expr: registration structure <-> points in real Euclidean space; mutually adjacent at separation 2 (unit spheres in contact)
steps.what: the geometric-balance bridge -- registrations correspond to Euclidean points
steps.why: THE BRIDGE, added not derived. Where the pre-spatial relational floor ends and standing GEOMETRY begins: registrations CORRESPOND to points in a real Euclidean space (real coordinates + ordinary inner product, NOT Hilbert), mutually-adjacent ones at a fixed minimum separation -- unit spheres in mutual contact, centers distance 2 apart. An EQUIVALENCE, not an identity (a registration is not a point). It rests on container 01's non-overlap adjacency for what 'mutually adjacent' means. Held as the postulate; this is exactly the AXIOM maths 4 files.

steps.check: each equidistant config has Gram diag D, off-diag D/2
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the Gram is fixed by equidistance alone)
steps.what: equidistant points -> the Gram of differences is (D/2)(I + J) -- polarization
steps.why: fix a base point; the N-1 difference vectors each have norm^2 = the common distance^2 D (each p_i is at distance^2 D from p_0), and pairwise inner product D/2 by polarization (<v_i,v_j> = (|v_i|^2 + |v_j|^2 - |v_i - v_j|^2)/2 = (D + D - D)/2, since |p_i - p_j|^2 = D too). So the Gram matrix is D on the diagonal, D/2 off it = (D/2)(I + J). Verified exactly on concrete configs (line, tetrahedron).

steps.check: det(I+J)_{N-1} = N for N=2..7; det(Gram) nonzero on the configs
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the determinant is a fixed nonzero value)
steps.why: the eigenvalues of I + J on R^{N-1} are N (once, eigenvector all-ones) and 1 (multiplicity N-2), so det(I + J)_{N-1} = N; scaling by D/2 gives det(Gram) = N*(D/2)^{N-1}. For D > 0 this is strictly positive, hence NONZERO. Verified exactly: det(I+J) = N for N = 2..7, and det(Gram) matches on the concrete configs. This nonzero Gram is the whole content of affine independence.

steps.check: dim >= N-1 for N=2,3,4 via the nonzero Gram determinant
steps.determines: the LOWER bound dim >= N-1 (the upper bound is NOT claimed -- see 03)
steps.expr: det(Gram) != 0 => the N-1 differences are independent => the N points are affinely independent => ambient dim >= N-1
steps.what: nonzero Gram => affinely independent => dim >= N-1 (the tetrahedron is 3-D)
steps.why: a nonzero Gram determinant means the N-1 difference vectors are linearly independent, so the N equidistant points are affinely independent, so the ambient space has dimension at least N-1. Concretely: 2 points force d>=1 (a line), 3 force d>=2 (a plane), 4 force d>=3 (a volume). This is the DERIVATION of 'the tetrahedron is genuinely 3-dimensional' -- replacing the retracted RUNG3-TETRAHEDRON-MINIMUM stipulation. The kernel checks the Gram determinants (N=2,3,4); the general det != 0 => independent => dim bound is the standard linear-algebra fact, now PROVED IN-REPO at Container05.EquidistantDimensionReal (Mathlib; see 5.6).

steps.why: the geometry is a CORRESPONDENCE the registration structure admits, not a claim that a registration IS a point in R^n. The relational floor (rungs 0-4.5) remains the substrate; the Euclidean picture is its faithful image across the bridge. This guards against reifying the coordinates -- 'all of math is a language ... to describe a thing' (Kevin). Held as the reading, capped.
